title: Reel: the first three seconds, one second at a time
hook: The first three seconds of your ad, one second at a time.
caption:
The first three seconds of your ad, one second at a time.

Second 1: show something your running ads haven't shown.
Second 2: put the buyer or their problem on screen.
Second 3: give the reason to stay. Say what they will get by the end, in words on screen.

Why the opening gets this much care: in our analysis of new video ads launched May to September 2026, a new message over a familiar first shot got 16% less first-month spend.

Save this for your next edit. Follow @galvor.ai.

script.setup: Idea: a video editor or creative strategist who puts the new idea in the middle of the ad learns what each of the first three seconds has to do. On-screen title: Your ad's first three seconds. Expectation set: a breakdown of an opening. The script beats it with a number from our analysis and a job for each second. Outline: familiar first shot costs spend (our finding); second one, a new picture; second two, the buyer or problem (second-best); second three, the reason to stay (best).

scenes.visual: A dummy ad plays on a phone with a three-second timer bar above it, split into three blocks.
scenes.voiceover: The first three seconds of your ad, one second at a time.

scenes.visual: The opening is drawn as wrapping paper around a box labelled message.
scenes.voiceover: The common view: the message matters, the opening is packaging.

scenes.visual: A new line of copy sits over a familiar-looking opening frame. A bar shrinks. Small source line: Galvor analysis, ads launched May–Sep 2026.
scenes.voiceover: New message, familiar first shot: sixteen percent less first-month spend.

scenes.visual: The timer bar returns, its three blocks numbered.
scenes.voiceover: So here's what each second has to do.

scenes.visual: Block one lights up. The opening frame changes to a clearly different picture.
scenes.voiceover: Second one: show something your running ads haven't shown.

scenes.visual: Block two lights up. A person, or a close-up of the problem, fills the frame.
scenes.voiceover: Second two: put the buyer or their problem on screen.

scenes.visual: Block three lights up and pulses.
scenes.voiceover: Second three is the one most ads skip: the reason to stay.

scenes.visual: A short line of text appears on the ad itself, promising what the viewer will get.
scenes.voiceover: Say what they'll get by the end. In words, on screen.

scenes.visual: End card with the three blocks ticked and the Galvor logo. Chime.
scenes.voiceover: Win three seconds, earn the rest. Follow @galvor.ai.

script.music: Light instrumental bed, low under the voice. Soft chime on the end card only.
script.notes: AI voiceover over motion graphics. No presenter and no first person singular. Captions burned in for muted viewing. Use dummy ad tiles only, never a client account or name. Number: 16% less first-month spend for a new message over a familiar first shot, Galvor analysis of every new video ad launched May–Sep 2026 across brands we work with (Decoded #3). Show the source line on screen in scene 3. Use a dummy ad made for this reel, never a client's ad.

slides.headline: Win three seconds. *Then the message gets its chance.*
slides.sub: Save this for your next edit.

notes:
Kept the topic and gave each second one job. Number used: 16% less first-month spend (Galvor analysis of ads launched May–Sep 2026). To confirm with Raj: 'the one most ads skip' in scene 7 is a view, not a measured finding; soften to 'the one that is easy to skip' if he prefers. Slide 1 is the cover, slide 2 the end card.
